claude.sample_unit: LLM responses (100 virtual NVAF patient cases x 9 LLMs)

links.outcome: Consistency of LLM outputs across 3 repeated sessions on 15 cases
links.effect: Percentage agreement varied widely; e.g., HAS-BLED agreement 26.67% (DeepSeek-R1), 40% (ChatGPT-4o Deep Research), 46.67% (DeepSeek-V3); regimen agreement 60-80%.
links.quote: The consistency levels of the 3 models varied across tasks; although ChatGPT-4o Deep Research demonstrated relatively stable performance in most domains, its consistency was comparatively lower in the anticoagulation regimen task.

links.outcome: LLM HAS-BLED scoring accuracy against multidisciplinary team reference standard
links.effect: HAS-BLED accuracy was low across all models (8%-51%); best model ChatGPT-4o Deep Research reached only 51%.
links.quote: In contrast, performance of the HAS-BLED scoring task was suboptimal for all models; even the best-performing model (ChatGPT-4o Deep Research) achieved an accuracy of only 51%.

links.outcome: HAS-BLED scoring accuracy before vs after prompt optimization with guideline criteria
links.effect: DeepSeek-R1 accuracy rose from 24% to 89%, ChatGPT-4o Deep Research from 51% to 95% (P < .001).
links.quote: Specifically, the accuracy of DeepSeek-R1 increased from 24% to 89%, while that of ChatGPT-4o Deep Research improved from 51% to 95%.

links.outcome: Comparison of 9 LLMs against each other on NVAF anticoagulation tasks
links.effect: Models varied substantially across 6 tasks; ChatGPT-4o Deep Research ranked first overall, DeepSeek-V3 lowest; no single model best across all tasks.
links.quote: The results showed that no single model performed optimally across all tasks.

links.outcome: Reliability of LLMs as stand-alone anticoagulation decision-makers
links.effect: Accuracy varied widely and HAS-BLED accuracy was low (8%-51%); authors conclude LLMs remain unsuitable as stand-alone decision-makers.
links.quote: At the current stage, LLMs are better suited as auxiliary tools for medical tasks rather than as independent decision-makers.

links.outcome: Errors in risk score calculation and dosing regimen accuracy
links.effect: Anticoagulation regimen (drug, dose, frequency) accuracy ranged 33%-89%; CHA2DS2-VASc accuracy 20%-100%; errors included double-counting and self-contradiction.
links.quote: In contrast, performance of the HAS-BLED scoring task was suboptimal for all models; even the best-performing model (ChatGPT-4o Deep Research) achieved an accuracy of only 51%.

unlisted_practices: Comparing base vs reasoning (Deep Think) vs web-retrieval (Deep Research) LLM variants

links.outcome: Stand-alone anticoagulation decision-making
links.effect: No single model was optimal; HAS-BLED accuracy 8%-51%, regimen selection 33%-89%, monitoring mean 2.55-4.98.
links.quote: At present, LLMs may serve as valuable adjuncts to clinical practice but remain unsuitable for use as stand-alone decision-makers.

links.outcome: Repeated-query output consistency
links.effect: Agreement ranged 26.67%-100.00%; ChatGPT-4o Deep Research regimen agreement 60.00%, Fleiss’ kappa 0.547; DeepSeek-R1 HAS-BLED agreement 26.67%.
links.quote: The consistency levels of the 3 models varied across tasks; although ChatGPT-4o Deep Research demonstrated relatively stable performance in most domains, its consistency was comparatively lower in the anticoagulation regimen task.

links.outcome: Comparative performance across candidate LLMs
links.effect: Accuracy ranges: CHA2DS2-VASc 20%-100%, HAS-BLED 8%-51%, contraindication 25%-99%, anticoagulation option 61%-100%, regimen 33%-89%; monitoring mean 2.55-4.98; all P<.001.
links.quote: Across 900 responses, performance varied substantially across 6 clinical tasks.

links.outcome: HAS-BLED accuracy after adding guideline criteria to prompt
links.effect: After prompt modification, DeepSeek-R1 increased 24% to 89%; ChatGPT-4o Deep Research increased 51% to 95%; P < .001.
links.quote: Specifically, the accuracy of DeepSeek-R1 increased from 24% to 89%, while that of ChatGPT-4o Deep Research improved from 51% to 95%.

links.outcome: Anticoagulant regimen and dose accuracy
links.effect: Regimen correctness required drug, dose, and frequency; accuracy ranged 33% (DeepSeek-V3) to 89% (Claude Sonnet 4).
links.quote: For CHA 2 DS 2 -VASc scoring, anticoagulation regimen selection, and medication monitoring recommendation tasks, performance differences across models were particularly pronounced: in CHA 2 DS 2 -VASc scoring, the lowest accuracy was observed for Qwen3 (20%), whereas the highest was achieved by ChatGPT-4o Deep Research (100%); in anticoagulation regimen selection, DeepSeek-V3 had the lowest accuracy (33%), and Claude Sonnet 4 had the highest (89%); in medication monitoring recommendations (evaluated using a Likert scale), DeepSeek-V3 had the lowest mean score (2.55), while ChatGPT-4o Deep Research had the highest (4.98).

links.outcome: Accuracy against MDT consensus
links.effect: HAS-BLED accuracy ranged 8.00%-51.00%; CHA2DS2-VASc 20.00%-100.00%; contraindication 25.00%-99.00%; anticoagulation regimen 33.00%-89.00% (all P<.001).
links.quote: In contrast, performance of the HAS-BLED scoring task was suboptimal for all models; even the best-performing model (ChatGPT-4o Deep Research) achieved an accuracy of only 51%.

links.outcome: consistency of model outputs across repeated queries over time
links.effect: Agreement across 3 repeated queries was 26.67%-60.00% for HAS-BLED, 60.00%-80.00% for anticoagulation regimen, and varied across models (DeepSeek-V3 46.67%-93.33%, DeepSeek-R1 26.67%-80.00%, ChatGPT-4o Deep Research 40.00%-100.00%).
links.quote: The consistency levels of the 3 models varied across tasks; although ChatGPT-4o Deep Research demonstrated relatively stable performance in most domains, its consistency was comparatively lower in the anticoagulation regimen task.

links.outcome: HAS-BLED scoring accuracy with vs without guideline criteria in prompt
links.effect: HAS-BLED scoring accuracy improved significantly from 24% to 89% for DeepSeek-R1 and from 51% to 95% for ChatGPT-4o Deep Research following prompt optimization with guideline criteria (P < .001).
links.quote: Specifically, the accuracy of DeepSeek-R1 increased from 24% to 89%, while that of ChatGPT-4o Deep Research improved from 51% to 95%.
